 (BY SHRI ABHISHEK GILKE - ADVOCATE FOR THE RESPONDENT NO.1  AND RESPONDENT NO.2)
 T h is appeal coming on for order this day, t h e cou r  following:
 ORDER

Both these appeals have been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the award dated 24.07.2019 in MACC No. 111/2017 by Motor Accident Claim Tribunal,
Shajapur.
Both these appeals arises out of the common award dated 24.07.2019 and the question to be determined are of the same nature.
Accordingly, both the appeals are being disposed of simultaneously.
2. The main award is being passed in MA No. 5855 of 2019 and the MA No. 5899 of 2019 shall be governed by the same award.

3. MA No.5855 of 2019 has been preferred by the claimants for enhancement of four lacs compensation with 10% interest per annum, whereas MA No. 5899/2019 has been preferred by the National Insurance Company for the deduction of the awarded amount.

4. Facts in brief are that appellant in MA No. 5855 of 2019 has preferred an application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 for compensation of Rs. 30 lacs with 25% per annum interest regarding death of their son Zuber Khan aged 19 years and earning Rs. 7000/- per month by working as Cleaner.

On 21.03.2017 at 09:30 AM near the field of Meharban Banjara situated at village Patsiya, Police Station Maknod in motor accident by negligent driving of truck bearing No.
MP 09 KC 1580 by respondent No.2 and insured with respondent No.1.

sentences.text: contested the case but respondent No.2 did not mark his presence before the Tribunal and the case has been proceeded ex-parte against him.
5. The Tribunal framed the issues, recorded the evidence of Smt Abeda Bi (PW-1) and Raoof Kha (PW-2) and admitted the documents Exhibit-P-1 to Exhibit-P-17 (C).
The respondents did not produce any evidence.

6. Tribunal found proved that Zuber Khan died due to negligent driving of Truck bearing No. MP 09 KC1580 by respondent No.2, who was the owner of the truck also and the truck was insured by respondent No.1.

7. Tribunal also found proved that the age of Zuber Khan was 18 years at the time of accident on the basis of Mark Sheet of 5th class (Exhibit-P-11), but estimated his income Rs. 5000/- per month as calculated for twenty days according to per day wages of Rs. 250/- and deducted 1/4th for personal expenses and calculated the per annum of dependency to the tune of Rs. 45,000/- and applied the multiplier of 16 and the total loss of dependency was calculated as a sum of Rs. 7,20,000/- and Rs.15,000/- was allowed for funeral expenses and total compensation of Rs. 7,35,000/- was awarded to be paid jointly and severely at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of presentation of application till the date of recovery.
8.

Feeling aggrieved by the impugned award Appeal No. 5855 of 2019 has been preferred on the ground that the minimum wages on the date of accident was Rs. 7,125/- per month and so the Tribunal ought to have assessed the income of the deceased at least Rs. 7,125/-.
The Tribunal ought to have applied the multiplier of 18.
The amount in the head of future prospects has not been awarded.
The amount in the head of filial consortium has not been awarded.
The amount in the head of love and affection has not been awarded.

9. Miscellaneous Appeal No. 5899 of 2019 by National Insurance Company has been preferred on the ground that the Tribunal erred in not appreciating that deceased Zuber Khan was a bachelor and the only person who could be said to be dependent was his mother and in absence of any other dependent, deduction toward personal expenses could be only to the extent of half of the monthly income.
The Tribunal has not appreciated the evidence adduced by the parties in right perspective.
10. Only quantum of compensation is disputed therefore this Court is addressing only the quantum of compensation.
As per Exhibit-P-11, the income of the deceased was Rs. 7000/- per month.
It cant't not be more than that was claimed.
There is no reason to reduce the income assigning the reason that he would have worked only for twenty days.
Accordingly, income of Zuber Khan is assessed to the tune of Rs. 7000/- per month.
11. According to his date of birth is 06.04.1998, as per 12-C, the age of deceased Zuber Khan at the time of death was 18 years, 11 months and 15 d ays .

Considering the age of the deceased Zuber Khan, an amount of enhancement of 40% in the head of future prospects is also allowed and the multiplier of 18 instead of 16 has to be applied, but the deduction for personal expenses should be 50% as the Zuber Khan was bachelor.

So the loss of dependency calculated as Rs. 7000/-per month Smt. Abeda Bi vs National Insurance Company Limited on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35606582/
3 income plus 40% enhancement for future prospects comes to Rs. 9,800/- per month and 1,17,600/-
Rupees per annum and applying the multiplier of 18, it comes to Rs. 21,16,800/- and after deduction of 50% of personal expenses it finally comes to Rs. 10,58,400/-.

sentences.text:
The Tribunal has awarded only Rs.
7,20,000/- rupees, so the appellants are entitled for compensation of Rs. 3,38,400/- in the head of loss of dependency.
12. Tribunal has not awarded in the head of loss of consortium.
The claimants are awarded an amount of Rs. 80,000/- (40,000 x 2) in the head of filial consortium.
Tribunal has not awarded any amount in the head of loss of estate.

Accordingly, Rs. 15,000/- is awarded in the head of loss of estate and the appellants in MA No. 5855 of 2019 are entitled for further enhancement of Rs.
4,33,400/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of application i.e 10.07.2017 which shall be paid by respondents No.1 and 2 jointly and severally to appellants of MA No. 5855 of 2019.

13. The appellants have valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.4 lakhs and paid the Court fee accordingly, however, for the remaining amount, the Court fee shall be paid by the appellants within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months, the claimant shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
14. Accordingly, both the appeals are disposed off.
15. True copy of this order be placed in the other connected matter.

(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE rashmi Smt. Abeda Bi vs National Insurance Company Limited on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35606582/
